code: function findUser(id) { return users.find(u => u.id === id); }
expected: Linear search O(n) on potentially large array. Consider using a Map or object for O(1) lookups: const userMap = new Map(users.map(u => [u.id, u])). For databases, ensure proper indexing on id column.

code: const results = []; for (let i = 0; i < data.length; i++) { results.push(await processItem(data[i])); }
expected: Sequential async operations cause unnecessary delays. Use Promise.all() for parallel execution: await Promise.all(data.map(processItem)). Consider rate limiting if API has concurrency restrictions.
Inefficient DOM manipulation! Using += innerHTML causes browser to reparse entire content. Use DocumentFragment or insertAdjacentHTML. Better yet, use virtual DOM framework for complex updates.

Inefficient and lossy cloning. Loses functions, dates, undefined, symbols. For deep clones, use structuredClone() (modern browsers) or libraries like lodash.cloneDeep(). For shallow clones, use spread operator.

code: const filtered = data.filter(x => x.active).map(x => x.name).filter(n => n.length > 5);
expected: Multiple array iterations! Combine operations into single pass. Use reduce or a single filter with map: data.filter(x => x.active && x.name.length > 5).map(x => x.name) or use for...of loop.

Excessive polling frequency causes performance issues. 100ms interval is too aggressive. Consider: increase interval (1000-5000ms), use WebSockets for real-time updates, or implement exponential backoff.

code: const sorted = array.sort(); const reversed = array.reverse();
expected: Unintended mutation! sort() and reverse() modify original array. Create copies first: const sorted = [...array].sort(). Also, default sort() is lexicographic - provide compare function for numbers.

code: function calculateFib(n) { if (n <= 1) return n; return calculateFib(n-1) + calculateFib(n-2); }
expected: Exponential time complexity O(2^n)! Highly inefficient for large n. Use memoization, dynamic programming, or iterative approach. Consider: const fib = (n, memo = {}) => memo[n] || (memo[n] = n <= 1 ? n : fib(n-1, memo) + fib(n-2, memo)).

code: const regex = new RegExp(pattern); for (let item of items) { if (regex.test(item)) { matches.push(item); } }
expected: Good practice creating regex once outside loop. However, test() with global flag has stateful lastIndex. For filtering, consider items.filter(item => regex.test(item)) but reset lastIndex or use match() instead.

Importing entire lodash library adds ~70KB to bundle. Use tree-shakeable imports: import debounce from 'lodash/debounce' or lodash-es. Consider native alternatives or smaller libraries for specific functions.
